$comment: THE canonical design tokens. Edit here and nowhere else.
REWRITTEN 2026-09-09 to carry the CURRENT design system.
This file used to hold an older palette (white ground, near-black
accent, good/warn/correction) that fed only the paused apps/mobile.
apps/frontend deliberately opted out of it and grew its own token
layer, which is the system the product actually looks like now —
TRACKER D36 recorded unifying them as an open decision. A third
client arriving is the moment to close it, because generating a
Flutter theme from the old file would have shipped the app looking
like a design the web app had already moved away from. That is drift
on day one, and drift is the whole reason this pipeline exists.
So the values below are transcribed from apps/frontend's token layer
(src/styles/globals.css and tailwind.config.ts), which is now the
source rather than a second opinion.
HOW THE THREE CONSUMERS RELATE
apps/frontend  declares these in globals.css. sync-tokens.mjs does
NOT overwrite that file — it CHECKS that it agrees,
so a working, tested stylesheet is never rewritten by
a generator, and a divergence still fails the build.
apps/app       generated: lib/theme/generated_tokens.dart.
apps/mobile    no longer a target. That app is superseded by
apps/app and its generated file is frozen where it
is; regenerating it would only repaint an app that is
on its way out.
Colours are the platform's neutral base. A family overrides only the
brand ramp (CLAUDE.md #7) — the ground, the ink, the lines, the
verification green and the danger red stay the platform's, because a
family may colour its signature and may not repaint the product.
Contrast: every foreground token clears 4.5:1 against both canvas and
surface. inkFaint is the documented exception and is used only for
decoration that is never the sole carrier of meaning.
$commentDark: The provider surface inverts to a dark header (design addendum §2:
two roles, two surfaces). It is a SCOPE, not a second theme — the
same components render inside it, and only the tokens listed here
change. On the web it is the .surface-dark class; in Flutter it is a
Theme override on the subtree, which is the same idea in the idiom
$commentType: A 15px body: small enough to be dense, large enough to read on a
mid-range Android at arm's length. letterSpacing is in em, as CSS
declares it; the Dart emitter multiplies by fontSize, because Flutter
`weight` is the DEFAULT for the style, not a rule. A widget may set
another — the web does this with utility classes rather than baking
$commentElevation: Two-layer shadows tinted with the ink hue rather than pure black — a
black shadow on a cool grey ground reads as dirt. Structured rather
than a CSS string so Flutter can build BoxShadows from the same
numbers instead of a second set that drifts.
$commentTouch: A hard floor, not a suggestion. CLAUDE.md's Definition of Done.

font.$comment: Inter has no Devanagari coverage at all, so a second face is not optional. On mobile both are BUNDLED, never fetched: a font download on a patchy network is a blank screen.
